title: Letter from the Governor to Baroness Noakes DBE
summary: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey has responded to the House of Lords Financial Services Regulation Committee's January 2026 report on private markets, expressing support for the FPC's Private Markets System-Wide Exploratory Scenario (PM SWES), a multi-firm exercise launched to test how the private markets ecosystem behaves under stress. The letter confirms that UK banks collectively hold £173bn in banking book exposures to private market funds and highly-leveraged corporates backed by finance sponsors—equivalent to 8% of total committed limits across wholesale portfolios. The FPC also lowered its system-wide Tier 1 capital benchmark by one percentage point to approximately 13% of risk-weighted assets.
key_points: The FPC is conducting a Private Markets System-Wide Exploratory Scenario (PM SWES) involving alternative asset managers, private equity/credit funds, banks, insurers, and pension funds to test behavioural responses across the ecosystem under stress.

UK banks collectively hold £173bn in banking book exposures to private market funds and highly-leveraged sponsor-backed corporates, representing 8% of total committed limits across wholesale portfolios.
The PM SWES will run in two rounds during 2026, with a final report published in early 2027; interim findings will be released as key milestones are reached.
The FPC has reduced its system-wide Tier 1 capital benchmark from approximately 14% to around 13% of risk-weighted assets, reflecting reduced bank systemicness and improved risk measurement.
Private markets have grown significantly in the UK over two decades without being tested by a macroeconomic stress at their current scale, motivating the exploratory scenario.
The PRA is reviewing future reporting requirements for the non-bank financial institution sector, with particular focus on banks adequately understanding their own private market exposures.
why_it_matters: Private markets have become a significant and growing part of the UK financial system, yet their behaviour under macroeconomic stress is unknown at current scale. The PM SWES will fill critical data gaps and provide regulators with empirical grounding for future prudential policy. Banks' £173bn in private market exposures means that stress in this sector could propagate to the banking system, making this a material financial stability concern. The reduced capital benchmark suggests the FPC judges current resilience adequate but underscores that capital requirements must be calibrated carefully given long-run growth trade-offs.
market_structure_context: The letter directly addresses private market interconnections with the traditional banking system, including data gaps on banks' exposures to private market funds. The PM SWES is a market-structure tool specifically designed to evaluate system-wide behavioural responses under stress, involving multiple firm types (alternative asset managers, banks, insurers, pension funds). The FPC's capital benchmark adjustment reflects evolution in the financial system and improved risk measurement, both market structure considerations. The PRA's review of non-bank financial intermediation reporting requirements also falls squarely in this domain.
important_numbers: £173bn (UK banks' banking book exposures to private market funds and leveraged sponsor-backed corporates)
8% (of UK banks' total committed limits across wholesale portfolios)
13% (of risk-weighted assets — revised FPC system-wide Tier 1 capital benchmark)
1 percentage point (reduction in Tier 1 capital benchmark from prior level)
